Pattern Catalog

A reference catalog of 157 design patterns across 20 categories, plus 61 documented anti-patterns. Each pattern describes what it solves, when to use it, and how it works. Anti-patterns describe what to avoid and how to fix it.

  • Resilience
  • Data
  • Integration

  • Concurrency

How the system handles failure. See Resilience Patterns for layering, decision tree, and diagrams.

PatternWhat it does
Circuit BreakerStops calling a failing dependency, waits, then retries
BulkheadIsolates resources so one failure can’t exhaust everything
Retry with BackoffRetries with exponential delay and jitter
BackpressureFlow control when producer outpaces consumer
TimeoutUpper bound on outbound call duration
Graceful DegradationFallback response when a dependency is down

How data flows and is stored.

PatternWhat it does
Stream-to-StoreKafka consumer that writes to a store via buffered flushes
ETL/ELTBatch extract-transform-load for periodic processing
Event SourcingAppend-only event log as source of truth
CQRSSeparate read and write models

How services communicate.

PatternWhat it does
SagaDistributed transactions with compensating actions
ChoreographyEvent-driven, no central coordinator
API GatewayCentralized routing, auth, rate limiting

How code is organized.

PatternWhat it does
HexagonalPorts & adapters — decouple business logic from infra
DDDBounded contexts and domain aggregates
PluginExtensible core with registered components

How services start, run, and stop. See Lifecycle Patterns for state diagram and relationships.

PatternWhat it does
Service ManagerStartup, shutdown, health, graceful degradation
SidecarAuxiliary container for cross-cutting concerns
Scheduler / CronTriggers work at defined intervals
Workflow EngineCoordinates multi-step long-running processes
Strangler FigIncremental legacy system replacement
Database MigrationZero-downtime schema evolution

How parallel work is managed. See Concurrency Patterns for family diagram and decision guide.

PatternWhat it does
Actor ModelIsolated actors communicating via async messages
Producer-ConsumerDecouples work generation from processing via queues
Worker PoolFixed thread set pulling tasks from a shared queue
Reactor / Event LoopSingle-threaded I/O multiplexing
Read-Write LockMany concurrent readers, exclusive writer
Future / PromiseComposable async result values
